old: [Observed] The cascade, defined once. Stage 10's panel held 44 canonical codon-allele records, covering 41 distinct protein changes, in eight of the nine panel genes (pfcoronin contributed none); 21 were polymorphic in these 1,900 isolates; 6 of the 21 survived the ingest mask — the in_genomewide_scan field, defined at step10_resistance_panel.py:349 as numalt == 1, i.e. "would have survived the ingest filter"; and 3 reached the MAF-filtered scan matrix: pfdhfr C59R, pfdhfr N51I and pfaat1 S258L. The other three that passed the mask — pfcrt I356T, pfmdr1 D1246Y and pfcrt N326S — were then cut by MAF ≥ 0.05 at frequencies of 0.016, 0.011 and 0.008. These four numbers (44, 21, 6, 3) carry exactly this meaning wherever they appear in this manuscript, and the Abstract, Table S1, Section 6.8.3, Table S27 and Section 10.1 use this wording. In particular, the genome-wide scan did test three of the 21 polymorphic canonical codons, and no pfcrt, pfmdr1, pfdhps or pfk13 codon reached the MAF-filtered scan matrix — pfdhps because nothing survived the ingest mask, the others because what survived was either too rare (pfcrt I356T, pfcrt N326S and pfmdr1 D1246Y all passed the mask, reached the genome-wide store and were then cut by MAF at 0.016, 0.011 and 0.008) or monomorphic here (six pfk13 codons — F446I, P441L, Y493H, P553L, R561H, A675V — passed the mask and were fetched and found invariant). "Could not test at all" would be true of the final MAF-filtered scan matrix but false of ascertainment, which is the distinction this paragraph exists to draw, so the stronger wording is not used.

[Interpreted] Removing the polyclonal and clonally redundant isolates does not sharpen the structure. The silhouette by zone becomes slightly more negative, -0.020 against -0.016, which is the opposite of what would be seen if zone signal had been diluted by mixed infections. The small rises in trustworthiness are not evidence of better-resolved structure either: trustworthiness is computed on a sample 61 per cent smaller, where fewer isolates compete for each neighbour rank, and all six values still sit near 0.5. The one movement with a plain reading is the fall in the PCoA distance correlation, 0.322 to 0.287: the best-performing embedding reconstructs the distances slightly less well on the filtered set. A tight detached clump also remains in both the UMAP and the t-SNE panels of Figure S10a after the filters, so the 77 clonally redundant isolates and the polyclonal infections do not account for the clumping noted above; what does is still not established. The substantive gain here is one of reporting rather than of result: the ordinations can now be read on the same 1,900 isolates as the rest of Section 6, and on that sample they say what they said before.

Not an independent confirmation. The ordinations read a different input from Sections 6.4 to 6.7 — the published Pf8 mean genotype distance matrix, not the 3,916-SNP panel built here — so their agreement with those sections remains weak corroboration rather than a replication, and that is unchanged by the re-run. The sample objection, however, is now answered. The published run is computed over isolates that include the polyclonal and clonally redundant infections the rest of the analysis excludes, and polyclonality itself varies by zone (Section 6.2); restricting to the 1,900 analysis-set isolates removes that difference, and the near-zero silhouette survives it (Table S23a).

[Observed] The region-level Mantel test is significant in 2 of the 6 scenarios. It holds at the published thresholds (p = 0.0252) and marginally at MAF >= 0.02 (p = 0.0467). It fails at every relaxation of the Fws cut — p = 0.0874 at 0.90, 0.1687 at 0.80, 0.1792 with no monoclonality filter at all — and at MAF >= 0.01 (p = 0.0617). On the uncensored test, which Table S25 reports beside the floored one as standing practice, only the baseline clears 0.05: the MAF >= 0.02 scenario moves to p = 0.0502. The correlation itself does not simply weaken with every change — it is 0.432 and 0.434 in the two MAF scenarios, slightly above the baseline 0.427 — so what the relaxations mainly do is remove the permutation significance, not reverse the sign of the relationship.

Isolation by distance is withdrawn as a supported result. Two checks now bear on this test, they vary different things, and they agree. The leave-one-region-out jackknife (Table S26) finds it significant in 4 of 7 replicates, with significance collapsing whenever the region defining either end of the distance range is dropped — Upper East at the long end, Greater Accra or Eastern at the short end. The threshold sensitivity (Table S26a) finds it significant in 2 of 6 scenarios, and the relaxation that most directly tests the filter doing the most work — removing the Fws cut, which more than doubles the isolate count to 4,403 — moves p from 0.0252 to 0.1792. The honest statement is that the isolation-by-distance result holds at the published thresholds and almost nowhere else. The original manuscript's "weak but detectable" distance effect, retained through every earlier revision of this section including the one that reported the jackknife improving from 2 of 7 to 4 of 7, cannot be retained now, and the grading of this result in Sections 1, 7 and 10 as supported or moderately supported must change with it. This is the only positive spatial finding in the analysis and it is the one that did not survive the two checks the audit identified as most needed. It is reported here in full rather than deleted — the point estimate at the published thresholds is unchanged and a reader is entitled to it — but it should not be cited as evidence of distance-limited gene flow in Ghana.

old: [Interpreted] Three further qualifications apply to the Mantel tests themselves. First, the zone-level test has the larger correlation but the larger p-value, which is a power effect rather than a contradiction: with four populations only 4! = 24 distinct orderings exist, so the finest attainable p-value is 1/24 = 0.042 and significance requires essentially the single best permutation. The region-level test, with 5,040 orderings, is the better powered of the two and is the one reported above. Second, the zone-level p-value is reported as a Monte Carlo estimate from 9,999 permutations when the exact value is enumerable over all 24 orderings; this remains outstanding and the estimate should be replaced by the exact figure. Third, several of the 21 region pairs rest on small samples (Volta 21 isolates, Brong Ahafo 25, Eastern 34), and the scatter in Figure S12 is correspondingly wide.

Of the thirteen finite values, ten agree with a numerically stable tail to three significant figures. The other three, and both sentinels, are explained — and reproduced to the last printed digit — by computing the upper tail as 1 − Φ(z) in double precision. Immediately below 1 the doubles are spaced 1.1102 × 10⁻¹⁶ apart, so Φ(z) is quantised to multiples of that spacing and the tail recovered by subtraction can only take those values. old: [Observed] The zone contrasts in Table S27 inherit every design limitation of the FST analysis, including the one the original manuscript did not list. Zone is confounded with sequencing study. The confounding analysis is computed on the 4,905 QC-passing isolates, not on the 1,900-isolate analysis set, because study membership is a property of the full QC-passing cohort: those 4,905 come from 11 sequencing studies, of which Guinea savanna draws on six (n = 3,605), deciduous forest on five (n = 815, of which four, n = 811, are large enough to enter the within-zone test — the fifth is a 4-isolate study), coastal savanna on two (n = 435) and the Transitional zone on a single study (1083-PF-GH-CONWAY, n = 50); 435 + 815 + 3,605 + 50 = 4,905. Four of the six zone pairs share no partner study at all, among them coastal savanna against Guinea savanna, which is the pair carrying both the maximum FST and every marker contrast reported above. Study-associated heterogeneity within these data is demonstrable rather than hypothetical — holding zone constant, call rate differs between studies within Guinea savanna at p = 2.8e-197 (Kruskal–Wallis, 6 studies, n = 3,605) and within deciduous forest at p = 7.7e-88 (4 studies, n = 811); because collection year, finer geography and recruitment also differ between studies inside a zone, this is heterogeneity associated with study rather than a demonstrated technical cause. A zone difference in marker frequency and a study difference in marker frequency are not separable here for the pairs that carry the largest effects.

FST, ADMIXTURE and TreeMix are three summaries of one genotype matrix: all three are computed from the same per-zone allele counts, and at this level of differentiation a four-population covariance matrix and the pairwise FST matrix are near-deterministic functions of each other. Only the ordinations use a different input — MalariaGEN's published Pf8 genotype-distance matrix — and they are now computed on the same 1,900 isolates as everything else, because stage 3 has been re-run on the analysis set (silhouette by zone −0.020; Table S36 row 21, Figure S20). Those six scenarios are not independent lines either — they are the same pipeline on overlapping data — but they establish that the headline does not depend on the analyst's threshold choices, which is a different and more useful thing. The region-level Mantel test does not share that robustness, and it has to be given up. It is a fourth summary of the same matrix, computed from region-level FST, so it was never independent of the others; and it is significant in only 2 of 6 threshold scenarios and 4 of 7 leave-one-region-out replicates, so it cannot be cited as a converging line at all (Table S33, row 1). old: Test isolation by distance properly, or stop reporting it as a finding. The region-level Mantel test on 21 pairs is at the limit of what Pf8's Ghanaian metadata supports, and it fails at four of the six threshold settings tried. Re-running it will not help. Two routes would: district- or site-level coordinates wherever the metadata carries them, which raises both the number of populations and the number of pairs; and a continuous-space method that does not require populations to be defined at all. Either is a new analysis rather than a robustness check, and neither is cheap. Until one is done the manuscript should carry near-panmixia as its spatial result and isolation by distance only as a non-robust observation, which is how Section 10.1 and Table S39 now report it.

old: [Observed] This appendix exists for traceability, and it now records three rounds. Round one, 9–10 October 2026: an adversarial multi-agent audit. Eight reviewers working across separate dimensions raised 110 findings, each of which was then put to three independent verifiers prompted to refute it and defaulting to refuted where they could not substantiate the claim. A finding counts as confirmed only where at least two of three verifiers failed to refute it after checking the code, data or outputs themselves. Sixty-one findings were confirmed — 14 high severity, 31 medium, 16 low — with 19 disputed and 21 refuted. Thirty verifications in the reproducibility dimension were lost to a rate limit and are recorded as unverified rather than confirmed. Seven confirmed defects required code changes; stages 4 to 9 were re-run on 10 October 2026 with all seven in place. Round two, 10 October 2026: an external critique of the corrected manuscript. It raised five points. All five were upheld and four were defects in the analysis code, not in the prose — in the resistance panel that round one had introduced to fix its own largest finding. The panel was rebuilt as scripts/step12_codon_panel.py and every resistance number in this revision was read from that script's outputs. This is the fourth consecutive round in which a correction contained its own defect, and the pattern is consistent: each layer was checked for internal consistency against our own outputs, and what escaped was external correctness — whether the marker list matched an authoritative source, whether the annotation direction matched the reference genome, whether a co-occurrence claim had co-occurrence data behind it. The verification architecture was built to catch stale numbers, and it did. It was not built to ask whether the inputs were the right ones. Round three, 10 October 2026: the four outstanding robustness checks. This round was not an audit of the manuscript but the execution of four items that Section 10.4 carried as outstanding, and it is recorded here because one of them overturned a conclusion instead of confirming it. The Fws and MAF sensitivity analysis (scripts/step13_sensitivity.py) withdrew isolation by distance as a supported result — significant in two of six threshold scenarios — and, from the same six runs, made near-panmixia the best-evidenced conclusion in the manuscript. The outlier quality check cleared the exported-protein artefact concern and downgraded two chromosome-11 SNPs on an ExcessHet and InbreedingCoeff signal. Stage 3 was re-run on the analysis set. The GeoJSON provenance cannot be closed analytically and remains open. Round three found no defect in the prose and none in the analysis code; what it found was that a published result depended on the thresholds that produced it. Two integrity incidents occurred during the round and are registered as rows 13 and 14 of Table S43 rather than left in the logs.

Table S43. Confirmed defects that required code changes: eight from the internal audit (the eighth found by the re-run itself), four from the external critique, and two integrity incidents from the robustness round of 10 October 2026. All fourteen are fixed. Defects 1-8 were re-run on 10 October 2026; defects 9-12 are fixed in step12_codon_panel.py, whose outputs supersede step10's. Rows 13 and 14 are operational rather than analytical: neither changed a reported number, and they are registered here rather than left in the logs because a defect register that records only the defects that changed a number is not a defect register.

Table S44. Confirmed defects corrected in the text rather than in code, from both rounds. No re-run was needed for any of them with one exception, which is noted rather than hidden: the pfcrt codon 75 entry's correction comes from the panel rebuild recorded as defect 9 of Table S43 and did require a re-run; it is repeated here because the wording it replaces was prose. The four entries shown in bold were raised by the external critique, whose five points are otherwise recorded as defects 9-12 of Table S43; on the critique's own four-code/one-prose split only the pfaat1 interpretation and the gene-level WHO tier labels are text-only, so the bold marks here should not be read as four further text-only defects.

Three items have come off this list since the previous version, all in the robustness round of 10 October 2026: the Fws and MAF sensitivity analyses, now reported in Section 10.1 and Table S38; the mapping-quality check at the outlier positions, now in Section 10.1 and results/outlier_quality_check.csv; and the re-run of Stage 3 on the analysis set, now Figure S22. What remains: the functional-enrichment permutation test for the outlier gene set; the temporal control at a single collection year; the robustness join against an authoritative six-zone Ghana layer; the recomputation of the zone-pair study overlap on the 1,900-isolate set; independent corroboration of the 32 panel codons MalariaGEN does not publish per sample; and, added by the robustness round, a read-level depth check at Pf3D7_11_v3:1054078 and Pf3D7_11_v3:1054447, without which two of the 19 outliers stay qualified.
